metadata.description: Parameter sensitivity atlas: foot radius vs leg scale at flat terrain (slope=0)
metadata.note: Based on documented claims in VERSIONS.md line 17, 20. Data extracted from existing CSV file.

y_axis.description: Leg length scaling factor (thigh + shank proportional scaling)

key_findings.1_narrow_success_basin: Only 16.7% (6/36) of parameter space yields stable gait
key_findings.2_geometric_sensitivity: Success concentrated in mid-range foot_radius (0.034-0.046m) with varied leg_scale
key_findings.3_failure_modes: Stuck (36%) and fall_down (47%) dominate failure modes
key_findings.4_best_performance: Highest forward distance at (foot=0.046m, leg=1.06) with 5.736m traveled
key_findings.5_controller_fragility: V10 PD controller shows high sensitivity to geometric parameters

baseline_parameters.note: Baseline not in grid but close to successful region at (0.038, 0.98)

comparison_to_baseline.interpretation: Success region clusters around baseline values but tolerance is narrow

decision_gate_context.verdict: Low success rate (16.7%) indicates V10 controller operates near isolated stability point, not robust basin
decision_gate_context.implication: Hardware manufacturing tolerances may be too tight - controller redesign needed (V13.5/V13.6)
decision_gate_context.next_steps: V13.6 event-driven FSM or V15 compliant actuation to widen success basin

reporting_guidance.academic_integrity: Report as 'parameter sensitivity analysis reveals narrow stability region (16.7% success)'
reporting_guidance.classification: Quasi-passive gait (active hip/knee stabilization, NOT pure passive)
reporting_guidance.honest_representation: This demonstrates controller fragility, not robustness - report failure rate honestly
